title: WAIT… YOU CAN GROW UP WITH JESUS—AND STILL NOT BELIEVE IN HIM.
paragraphs: WAIT… YOU CAN GROW UP WITH JESUS—AND STILL NOT BELIEVE IN HIM.

You can hear His name every day…
see His works…
sit at the same table—

They saw Him wake up.
They heard Him pray.
They watched Him live without sin—
Because this isn’t just their story.

Close to church.
Close to truth.
Close to the presence of God—
And here’s the tension most people don’t want to face:
Familiarity can become the greatest form of blindness.
Still saying, “I’ll follow… but on my terms.”
Scripture doesn’t hide this uncomfortable truth:
“Isn’t this the carpenter’s son? … Aren’t his brothers James, Joseph, Simon and Judas? Aren’t all his sisters with us?” — Matthew 13:55–56

They reduced the Son of God…
to something ordinary.
“For even his own brothers did not believe in him.” — John 7:5
This is the danger of pride.

But pride will keep you near Jesus…
while your heart stays miles away.
Some of us don’t reject Jesus outright.
But Jesus is not looking for admiration.
And here’s the turning point—the moment everything shifts:

Because when Jesus rose from the grave,
He didn’t just prove a point.
From brother… to servant of the Lord.

The man who once doubted…
now warns about pride.
“Submit yourselves, then, to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.” — James 4:7
You are not saved because you are close to Jesus.
You are saved when you repent and believe in Him.
Sin is not just what you do.
It’s the posture of a heart that says:
The same Jesus misunderstood in His own home—
lived the life you couldn’t live…
and rose again so you could be made new.
Stop treating Jesus like He’s common.
Stop keeping Him at a distance while claiming you’re “close.”
Of knowing about Him without knowing Him.
Because even His own brothers had to make a choice.
Let the risen Christ meet you—not as a concept…
Let it be your first step.
